sentences.text:
Opposite Party
 Mr. M.K. Mohanty, Addl. Pp
 Coram:
 Justice G. Satapathy
 Order(Oral)
08.09.2025 Order No.
08. 1.

This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is an application U/S.483 of BNSS by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Chandbali PS Case No. 277 of 2018 corresponding to Special(POCSO) Case No.110 of 2018 pending in the file of learned Adhoc Addl. District and Sessions Judge(FTSC), Bhadrak for commission of offences punishable U/Ss.363/366/376(2)(n) of the IPC r/w Section 6 of POCSO Act, on the main allegation of kidnapping the victim and committing rape and aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
3. Heard, Mr. Kshirod Kumar Pahil, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. M.K. Mohanty,
learned Addl. Public Prosecutor in the matter and perused the record, but none appears for the victim despite being duly informed as apprised by learned Addl. PP.

4. After having considered the rival submissions and taking into consideration the nature and gravity of the offence as alleged against the petitioner vis-a- vis the accusations sought to be brought against him and regard being had to the pre-trial detention of the petitioner in custody since 19.03.2024 with submission of charge sheet in the meantime and taking into account the conduct of the Petitioner in not misusing the concession so granted to him in the form of interim bail as claimed and keeping in view the other circumstances on record in entirety including the statement of the victim, this Court without expressing any view on merits admits the Petitioner to bail.

sentences.text: Hence, the bail application of the Petitioner stands allowed and the Petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) only with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it.

The aforesaid order is subject to verification of the surrender of the Petitioner to the custody after availing the interim bail and if he is found to have not surrendered to the custody or has surrendered to the custody after expiry of the interim bail, the benefit of this order shall not be extended to him without seeking leave of this Court.
6. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy) Judge Priyajit Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA Chagulu @ Pratap Sethi vs State Of Odisha ...
